rules.rule: Research preview, API/hosted availability, limited rollout, public product availability, weight release, and later family update are separate events unless a primary source explicitly establishes simultaneity.
rules.reason: Retrospective reconstruction must not back-project later availability into an earlier announcement.

rules.rule: Normalize openness separately across weights, inference/code, training recipe/logs, training data, license terms, and reproducibility artifacts.
rules.reason: The labels open, open-weight, and open-source were used heterogeneously during 2024-H1.

rules.rule: Vendor-published benchmark comparisons remain attributed vendor claims unless independently reproduced in accepted Evidence.
rules.reason: Architecture must not convert launch-material benchmark tables into neutral comparative facts.

rules.rule: Treat GPT-4o's native multimodal model design separately from staged modality/product availability at launch.
rules.reason: Model architecture and user-accessible modalities did not become available on one identical lifecycle boundary.

rules.rule: Preserve the February Gemini 1.5 context-window announcement and limited long-context preview separately from May Gemini 1.5 Flash and later expanded-context preview/waitlist events; do not back-project later limits to February.
rules.reason: Long-context capability and access expanded during the half-year.

rules.rule: Treat the May Chameleon research paper and June public research release as distinct events, and do not infer that every paper capability or checkpoint was publicly released.
rules.reason: Research capability scope and released artifact scope differ.

rules.rule: Keep the February Stable Diffusion 3 preview, any separately evidenced API availability, and the June Stable Diffusion 3 Medium release as distinct lifecycle events.
rules.reason: Preview, hosted use, and downloadable model release are not interchangeable.

rules.rule: Normalize February OLMo launch and April OLMo 1.7 as an evolving open-training lineage rather than unrelated releases or one timeless artifact.
rules.reason: The Special should capture both openness artifacts and within-period model improvement.

rules.rule: Normalize Command R, tool-use support, and Command R+ as related but distinct model/tool/deployment events.
rules.reason: RAG orientation, tool use, and family progression occurred on separate dates and layers.

rules.rule: For living first-party pages or repositories, use release-bounded 2024-H1 claims and chronology only; later edits may inform current reconstruction but cannot be attributed to the covered date without dated evidence.
rules.reason: Current-reconstruction methodology must preserve historical event time.

rules.rule: Preserve source distinctions among research preview, limited preview, waitlist, beta, hosted availability, public release, and open-weight release.
rules.reason: These terms encode materially different access states.

rules.rule: A paper and a first-party release page may support one story unit when they describe the same technical event, but paper evidence should support technical claims and release evidence should support release/availability chronology.
rules.reason: This prevents duplicate story units without collapsing source roles.

cross_period_questions: Which 2024-H1 technical axes became dominant product/deployment concerns in 2024-H2?
Which 2024-H1 previews crossed into public or open availability only after 2024-06-30?
Which releases described as open exposed only weights versus a broader reproducibility stack?
How did efficiency shift from model-size-only discussion toward active parameters, memory, serving, placement, and on-device execution?
architecture_constraints: Do not merge model capability, model availability, and product availability into one date.
Do not compare openness using one binary label.
Do not promote vendor benchmark leadership to an unqualified editorial claim.
When a current living source is used, carry an explicit H1 chronology boundary into Evidence and drafting.
